note: Weekend (Sat Nov 28 SGT) sweep covering the Fri Nov 27 US/Asia close plus pre-weekend Fed-blackout and oil-market developments. Fri 27 Nov was a major risk-on day (S&P +1.60%, Nasdaq +2.31%, VIX -11%) driven by two separate catalysts landing together: (1) China's State Council 'national team'/Central Huijin stabilization pledge, which drove a record 17.6% one-day CSI chip-index gain and lifted HK tech broadly, and (2) a mechanical short-covering bounce in gold/silver off a 15-month oversold low -- NOT a dovish-Fed or weak-dollar story, since Core PCE, Q3 GDP and jobless claims all printed hot and Fed officials (Waller, Williams) hardened their December-hike rhetoric the same day. 9 of 12 items below are dated Nov 26-27 (well above the freshness bar); the OPEC+ meeting (Sun Nov 30) and the Dec 8-9 FOMC blackout (started midnight ET Nov 28, per Arthur Hayes' weekend-selloff warning) are kept as imminent, dated catalysts rather than stale news. Crypto notably did NOT participate in Friday's rally and remains in 'Extreme Fear'.

items.headline: China's State Council 'national team'/Central Huijin pledge triggers record 17.6% one-day chip-stock rally; SMIC +16.4%, Hua Hong +20.7%, Hang Seng Tech +6.45%
items.summary: Premier Li Qiang chaired a rare midday State Council statement on Nov 27 calling for a bigger role for state-backed 'national team' investors -- the first time this language has appeared in an executive-meeting press release -- and urging Central Huijin Investment to act as a quasi-stabilization fund. The CSI Semiconductor Industry index closed up 17.60% (its biggest one-day gain on record), with SMIC (0981.HK) +16.39% to HK$53.40 and Hua Hong Semiconductor +20.69% to HK$78.15; the Hang Seng Index rose 2.11% to 22,694.77 with Tencent (0700.HK) +3.2% and Xiaomi (1810.HK) +3.8%.
items.actionable: This is the clearest bullish catalyst for the HK-tech sleeve in weeks -- a genuine policy-driven (not just risk-on-beta) rally in the chip names specifically -- but confirm it holds through Monday's full session rather than chasing a single holiday-thinned Friday print.

items.headline: Silver rockets ~6.9% to $44.44, gold +2% as oversold short-covering bounce follows 15-month low -- analysts warn it is not yet a trend reversal
items.summary: Spot silver surged roughly 6.2-6.9% to around $43.06-$44.44/oz and gold gained about 2% to roughly $3,565-3,670/oz on Nov 27, rebounding sharply from Tuesday's 15-month low of $38.18. Analysts at Kitco and GoldSilver.com characterize the move as short covering and mechanical mean-reversion off extreme oversold readings rather than a sentiment inflection -- domestic futures open interest fell even as prices rose, and the move came alongside rising, not falling, Treasury yields and a firmer dollar.
items.actionable: The levered silver position got a welcome relief rally, but because it is diagnosed as short-covering into a still-hawkish Fed (not a rates/dollar-driven reversal), this is a window to trim/de-risk into strength rather than confirmation that the squeeze risk has passed.

items.headline: Silver/gold miners post best week since August: GDX +15.8%, SILJ +8.79% on the day
items.summary: GDX (gold miners ETF) closed Friday at 79.18, up 15.8% on the week -- its best weekly performance since August -- while the Amplify Junior Silver Miners ETF (SILJ) jumped 8.79% (+$1.75) to close at $21.66 and the Global X Silver Miners ETF (SIL) rose 7.53%, both riding the underlying metals bounce plus the broader risk-on wave.
items.actionable: Miners outperformed the metals themselves (operating leverage working in the portfolio's favor), but a 15-16% weekly move in GDX this far above the metal's own gain is exactly the kind of overextension that tends to mean-revert hard if the metals bounce stalls -- avoid adding to miner exposure at the week's highs.

items.headline: Hot Core PCE, upward-revised Q3 GDP and low jobless claims push December 9 Fed hike odds to 94-97%
items.summary: October core PCE printed +0.3% m/m/3.3% y/y, Q3 GDP's second estimate was revised up to +4.3% annualized (vs 3.5% consensus), and jobless claims fell to 189K (vs 201K forecast) -- all hotter than expected. Kalshi and Polymarket now price a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC at roughly 94-97% (Kalshi shows 93-95.7%, with CME Fed futures implying up to 99%), confirming the Fed remains firmly in a hiking, not cutting, cycle.
items.actionable: Friday's metals bounce happened despite, not because of, the rates outlook -- near-certain odds of another hike on Dec 9 keep the real-rate headwind for the silver/gold sleeve fully intact, so size the position for a resumption of pressure into the FOMC rather than a durable reversal.

items.headline: Fed's Waller floats a jumbo 50bp December hike, Williams won't rule out consecutive hikes
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on CNBC that if the Fed hikes 25bp in December it must clearly signal another 25bp in January, 'otherwise... you have to go 50 in December' -- effectively doubling down on a larger move and flagging at least two more hikes to come. NY Fed President John Williams separately told reporters on Nov 27 he would not exclude raising rates at consecutive meetings, reiterating inflation (forecast at 3.5% for 2026) remains too high and policy needs to stay restrictive.
items.actionable: Two separate Fed voices floating a bigger-or-longer hiking path on the same day gold/silver bounced is a warning that the rally is fighting the policy tape -- treat any further metals strength into the Dec 8-9 meeting with skepticism given this rhetoric came right before the pre-FOMC blackout silences further Fed commentary.

items.headline: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery push Brent to $96, oil's first weekly gain in a month
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed renewed strikes on Saudi Arabia's 550,000 b/d Ras Tanura refinery and the Jizan refinery; satellite imagery reportedly showed burnt storage tanks, though Riyadh has not confirmed damage. ICE Brent rose to roughly $95.90-$96/barrel (+8.1% over four trading days) and WTI climbed to about $84.65, putting crude on track for its first weekly gain in three weeks and reviving a geopolitical war-risk premium that defies earlier oversupply forecasts.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio ticker, but a sustained Brent move toward/through $100 would add an energy-driven inflation impulse on top of an already-hawkish Fed, reinforcing the case for staying defensive on the rate-sensitive precious-metals and HK-tech/SGX sleeves until this de-escalates.

items.headline: OPEC+ meets Sunday Nov 30 to set Q1 2027 output; Iraq and Kazakhstan dispute their new capacity ratings
items.summary: OPEC+ ministers hold a series of meetings this Sunday, Nov 30, expected to roll over Q1 2027 group output targets largely unchanged despite the group's first-ever production-capacity review. Iraq is pushing back on a preliminary 4.9m bpd capacity assessment (seeking recognition closer to 6m bpd versus its current 4.431m bpd quota) and Kazakhstan (1.628m bpd quota) is separately seeking a higher estimate, complicating the capacity-based quota framework for next year.
items.actionable: An unresolved capacity dispute raises the odds of a contentious or delayed OPEC+ outcome this weekend; a surprise output cut or further discord would add to the oil-driven inflation risk already flagged by the Houthi/Ras Tanura strikes, a modest incremental headwind for the hawkish-Fed thesis weighing on metals.

items.headline: China extends gallium/germanium/antimony export-suspension truce with the US to Jan 27, 2027
items.summary: China's Commerce Ministry announced on Nov 24 that it is extending its suspension of export bans on gallium, germanium, antimony and certain superhard materials to US buyers through Jan 27, 2027 -- a 61-day extension, far shorter than the year-long reprieve granted in November 2025. Existing export-licensing requirements and restrictions on supplies to US military end-users remain in force, and Beijing also extended relief on tighter end-use reviews for graphite shipments.
items.actionable: A shorter (61-day vs 1-year) truce extension signals Beijing is keeping this as active leverage rather than resolving it -- supportive near-term for the chip-supply-chain/HK-tech sleeve, but keep the rare-earth watchlist (MP, LYC.AX, UUUU) on alert for the late-January expiry as a recurring binary catalyst.

items.headline: Lynas rebounds 28% off October lows on record NdPr output as China's separate rare-earth-tech export truce stays unrenewed
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths (LYC.AX) shares jumped about 7% on Nov 26 to roughly A$13.70, extending a 28% rebound off their October low on record NdPr production and an 88% year-on-year rise in realized prices. This comes as a narrower, separate Chinese export pause covering certain processed rare-earth technologies expired Nov 10 with no renewal yet announced, leaving a continued supply-chain overhang specifically on US-based MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
items.actionable: Lynas's pricing power (NdPr +88% y/y) is a genuine fundamental tailwind for the rare-earth watchlist independent of any single truce headline, but the still-unrenewed technology-export pause keeps MP/USAR-specific supply risk live -- favor LYC.AX over MP-linked exposure until that pause is clarified.

items.headline: STI closes at session high 4,995.23 (+0.66%) as DBS and OCBC ride the global risk-on wave
items.summary: The Straits Times Index rose 32.59 points (+0.66%) to close at 4,995.23 on Friday, with gainers outnumbering losers 418 to 166 on S$1.6 billion of turnover. DBS gained 0.5% to S$66.15 and OCBC rose 0.7% to S$26.80, extending Thursday's gains as Singapore banks tracked the broader global equity rally.
items.actionable: The SGX bank sleeve is riding the same cross-asset risk-on wave as HK tech and precious metals rather than any bank-specific catalyst (Citi trimmed sector targets on Nov 19 citing softer loan growth/credit costs) -- fine to let it run but don't mistake this for a fundamental re-rating of DBS/OCBC.

items.headline: Singapore REITs rise but still down ~14% YTD; three blue-chip S-REITs now yield 7%+ at P/B lows
items.summary: The FTSE ST All-Share Real Estate REITs Index rose 0.61% to 635.92 on Nov 25, with ESR REIT offering the sector's highest trailing yield at 11.32%, even as the broader iEdge S-REIT Index remains down about 14.1% year-to-date versus the STI's +12.3%. CapitaLand Ascendas REIT, Mapletree Industrial Trust and Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust are all yielding 7%+ while trading near or at historical price-to-book lows.
items.actionable: The REIT sleeve's underperformance versus the STI (-14% vs +12% YTD) plus 7%+ yields at P/B lows is the kind of valuation gap the large cash pile exists to exploit -- worth screening CLAR/MIT/MPACT specifically for staged deployment if the yield/price-to-book gap persists into year-end.

items.headline: Crypto stuck in 'Extreme Fear' (11-12/100) as BTC holds near $60k, didn't join Friday's risk-on rally; Hayes warns of weekend selloff risk as Fed blackout begins
items.summary: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index rose only to 12 on Nov 27 from 11 the prior day, remaining in 'Extreme Fear' territory as Bitcoin held near $60,750 (ETF outflows in their 7th straight day) while equities, HK tech and precious metals all rallied hard the same day. Maelstrom CIO Arthur Hayes warned that absent a dovish Fed pivot before the pre-FOMC blackout began at midnight ET Nov 28 (running through Dec 10), 'this weekend could get spicy' for crypto, which trades through the weekend and could be sold into Monday's open.
items.actionable: Crypto's failure to participate in Friday's broad risk-on move -- plus a specific weekend-selloff warning right as the Fed goes dark into Dec 9 -- is a signal that risk appetite is narrower than headline equity/metals gains suggest; not a direct portfolio holding, but a useful cross-check against treating Friday's bounce as a broad-based regime change.
